fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Ishmael and his ten men come to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they eat a meal together there (Jeremiah 41:1). Ishmael was a member of the royal family and one of the king's chief officers. I think that meal had to be the quietest one ever served.

That's the one, baker. Ishmael killed "…the Chaldean soldiers who were there." along with the Jews who were with Gedaliah (Jeremiah 41:3). Gedaliah was the one whom the king of Babylon had appointed to govern the land (Jeremiah 41:2). That detail matters later in this story.
The Philistines are a good guess for a soldier question, baker. But the text names the Chaldean soldiers at Mizpah as the ones Ishmael killed (Jeremiah 41:3). No Philistines anywhere in this scene.

Not Baal, baker. The text says the grain offerings and frankincense were for "…the house of the LORD." (Jeremiah 41:5) These men came from Shechem, Shiloh and Samaria, and they were bringing their offerings to the LORD's house.

That's it, baker. Ishmael "…went out from Mizpah to meet them, weeping as he went." (Jeremiah 41:6) The text tells us what he did, and it doesn't say why he did it. What he did to those men next is heavy.
No laughing here, friend. The text says Ishmael went out "…weeping as he went." (Jeremiah 41:6) This is a heavy part of the story. Gedaliah already lies dead at this point (Jeremiah 41:2).

No songs on this road, baker. Ishmael went out to meet the eighty men "…weeping as he went." (Jeremiah 41:6) That's a sad scene even before the next verse. The eighty men came on the second day after Gedaliah was murdered (Jeremiah 41:4).

Not quite, friend. What Ishmael actually said was, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam." (Jeremiah 41:6) He didn't tell them to turn back. He called them toward Gedaliah, who was already dead, and when they came into the city, Ishmael and his men slaughtered them (Jeremiah 41:7).

Not quite, baker. The eighty men were already headed toward the house of the LORD (Jeremiah 41:5), so Ishmael didn't point them to Jerusalem. He said, "Come to Gedaliah son of Ahikam." (Jeremiah 41:6) In the city, Ishmael and his men slaughtered them and threw them into a cistern, though ten were spared (Jeremiah 41:7-8).

Right, baker. The ten men said they had hidden treasure in the field, and the text says "So he refrained from killing them with the others." (Jeremiah 41:8) The ten were spared, while the others were slaughtered and thrown into a cistern (Jeremiah 41:7). This is a heavy part of the story.

That's right, baker. Ishmael "…set off to cross over to the Ammonites." (Jeremiah 41:10) He took captive all the remnant of the people of Mizpah, including the daughters of the king. He was taking them away from Mizpah.
Moab is a good guess, baker, but it's not the one here. The text says Ishmael "…set off to cross over to the Ammonites." (Jeremiah 41:10) Moab doesn't come up in this passage.

That's the spot, baker. Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the armies with him took all their men and went to fight Ishmael, and they "…found him near the great pool in Gibeon." (Jeremiah 41:12) Gibeon is where they caught up with him.

The Jordan is a fair guess, friend, but it's not the place named. The text says Johanan's men found him "…near the great pool in Gibeon." (Jeremiah 41:12) Ishmael later escaped from Johanan with eight of his men and went to the Ammonites (Jeremiah 41:15).

Yes, baker. "When all the people with Ishmael saw Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the army with him, they rejoiced…" (Jeremiah 41:13) Then all the people Ishmael had taken captive at Mizpah turned and went over to Johanan (Jeremiah 41:14). I bet they were glad to see him.

Not quite, friend. The text says "…Ishmael son of Nethaniah and eight of his men escaped from Johanan…" (Jeremiah 41:15) He came to Mizpah with ten men (Jeremiah 41:1), so the number here is eight, not ten. Ishmael got away and went to the Ammonites.

Right, baker. "…Ishmael son of Nethaniah and eight of his men escaped from Johanan and went to the Ammonites." (Jeremiah 41:15) He came to Mizpah with ten men (Jeremiah 41:1), so the number is eight, not ten. The captives had turned and gone over to Johanan (Jeremiah 41:14).
Not Assyria, baker. Johanan and the people stopped at Geruth Chimham, near Bethlehem, "…in order to proceed into Egypt" (Jeremiah 41:17). Assyria isn't in this passage at all. Egypt was the plan.

Yes, baker. "…they were afraid of the Chaldeans because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land." (Jeremiah 41:18) Ishmael did the killing, and the people were the ones who felt the fear. They wanted to escape the Chaldeans.

Good memory on Johanan, friend, but this isn't it. He took his men and went to fight Ishmael (Jeremiah 41:12). The people feared the Chaldeans "…because Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land." (Jeremiah 41:18)

That's not what this passage says, baker. The text gives this reason: "…Ishmael son of Nethaniah had struck down Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land." (Jeremiah 41:18) Nothing here mentions the people stopping their service. The fear came because of what Ishmael did.
